title: rift
text: I'm a returning player.  Bought the game in 2011 and quickly leveled a rogue soul to 50 back then, maxed crafting to 300.  At some point, got bored and quit and went on to other games as happens in this industry.  And then it surfaced as a "free to play" MMO in my Steam queue.  I'm so glad that it did.  I decided to check it out and I'm hooked all over again. Just a few bullet points for the returning players / original box set purchases on what you'll find: - All my characters were on the trial server.  Easily transferred to a "real" server. - If you purchased a box set back in the day, you've already unlocked some of stuff new players have to pay for.  Namely, a few extra character slots, auction house access, extra bag slots.  That was nice to find out. -  Graphics have been much improved.  I logged in once before this and thought, no way, graphics are too dated.  Well, at some point along the line, they did a major overhaul.  It looks nice.  Could still use some optimization, won't lie.  I had to bring my settings down some and my machine is not a slouch.  But neverthless, still looks good. Here's what they have added off the top of my head since I played: -  Instant Adventures:  Think instant raids that level you quickly and give you quick coin.  If you don't relish the thought of leveling all over again, this is the way to level up quickly.  It's also a way to get a "dungeon group" of sorts since noone really does the dungeons actually in the game anymore.  Scales to your level starting from level 10. -  Minions.  New collectibles that go out and run adventures for you and bring back loot.  Sort of a card game as well. -  Costumes.  Unlock costume items as you find them and now make your character look how you want no matter what he/she is actually wearing (I love this, won't lie). -  Diminsions - Housing essentially.  You get a personal house and your guild can purchase one.  You can purchase diminsion items to decorate and your minion can go on missions to find items as well. -  Chronicles / Planar attunement - Honestly, no idea yet since this is all stuff you do with your character post level 50 and I actually started a new character to refresh my memory on how to play this game again. :P  I have looked it up and it seems as if it's a way of customizing your character even further however. At any rate, yes, the standard "pay" features are in this game as any: - Pay for extra soul walks or wait for a cool down. - Pay for extra bags - Pay for additional souls And so forth.  But they are not as obtrusive as other games.  And frankly, I've already purchased the $24.00 add on pack and might consider others in the future.  I like the game that much again.

text: I've been reading alot of negative reviews on this game. And they all have one thing in common. Every negative review states this is a pay to win game. No it's not, point blank period. The best gear cannot be bought with real money, that is a myth. Good gear can, but the best in slot is not on the real money store at all, check y'alls vision and know your facts first. Secondly, everything that can be bought with real money can be earned in game thru playing, which is why you should play the game in the first place. Let people blow there money and skip content, all good. Those players are not good with their classes and it shows, you know who bought their gear or got carried, let them continue to be bad. Now onto a postive review... This game has alot of good points about it. The questing system is alittle grindy but it's still good quests, good enough to keep your attention. The back story could use alot of work though, The raids are fun, and so are the dungeons. There is not a lack of raids or dungeons. If you don't want to quest, you can do instant adventures as well. And the best part about this game, is the content is no charge. They do however charge for 2 soul packs which aren't necessary to buy to be able to play. Also, you can buy an item called REX with in game currency, each REX gives you 1250 credits for the real money store. So anything in the store you can buy by learning the Auction House and using it to your advantange. This game is alot of fun for those who actually don't look at the negative reviews. Alot of biased comments are in here. And to be honest, there are alot of other MMO's on the market that restrict a F2P account so much you feel obligated to pay to compete. And there are others as well that are truly P2W. You can compete with players that use real money in this game easily. Anyone who tells you different is either a upset consumer with trion or just straight stupid. My 2 cents.... try the game out. If you like it play it, if you don't move on. Also, I've played way more than 105.1 hours. Alot of my time is thru Glyph and not Steam, so the time spent playing is very decieving.

title: rise of nations: extended edition
text: From ancient times all the way to the information age, Rise of Nations allows you to lead 18 different nations thru either the epic-scaled 'Conquer the World' gamestyle, or the classic 'quick game' style which is your basic RTS setup (1 base start, X-amt of resources, knock yourself out). Rise of Nations uses the tried and tested rock-paper-scissors method for unit counters but also adds in each individual nations bonuses and the abilities of Generals which combines overall for a decently complex multiplayer experience. Also given the fact that the most common playstyle in RoN (Rise of Nations) allows for not only military takeover wins, but also territory % wins,  and Wonder (massive buildings with unique bonuses) victories, RoN delivers quality strategy without sacrificing quantity (different nations and units to pick from). The Tech tree is straight forward, and is easy to pick up on (even for a rookie rts player), and rushing and economic boom strategies are both possible and competitive depending on which nation you pick. This game is a classic rts title that got revitalized on Steam for a reason: It's just.... brilliant if you're an rts fan,              get this title if you want to learn rts,          get this title if you're a collector of classics, get this title ENVOY RATED: 9/10

title: rise of the argonauts
text: This game would have been a lot better if there had been more combat. Seriously, only like 1/3 of the game was actual combat, while the rest was just walking around and talking to people, which gets tedious really quickly. Not that the combat was anything spectacular, just your standard hack'n'slash fare, only really, really easy. The enemies spend a lot of the time standing there and letting you attack them, i literally never used the block button. And if you do get down to low health, you can just walk away for a few seconds and your health regenerates. I didn't die until the final boss fight, and that's only because it took me a while to figure out how i was supposed to kill him. The only real positive was the interesting character progression system, where you complete deeds (save a villager, kill X enemies, etc.) and then dedicate those deeds to one of four gods to gain favour with those gods, and gaining enough favour with a specific god grants you a skill point to spend on that god's skill tree, with each god representing a different combat style. The story was OK, but the whole plot of the myth has been completely changed (instead of collecting the Fleece to restore his fathers kingdom, Jason only wants it to resurrect his dead wife) and all the characters are there, but they are completely different from their mythic counterparts, especially Medea, who instead of being a key part of the story, is just another Argonaut. All in all it was a pretty average game, but being a big fan of Greek myth i found it mildly enjoyable, despite being annoyed by the changes from the myth. However, I can't recommend it given how most of the game is spent in boring conversations. If there had been more action, I would recommend it, but sadly, there isn't enough to keep the game interesting. I also encountered frequent crashes at seemingly random points, but I can't say for sure if it's the game or my computer. However given that i can play more recent and far more graphically demanding titles than this, it seems likely that it's the game that's at fault.

text: Bought it on sale for about $2.00. Give it a chance. Took me a while to really get into it (6-7 hours) when the story started to make me give half a shieet and the combat felt like an iota more than just mashing X and Y. Pros: + Engaging story + Good voice acting + Semi-challenging boss fights + Cinematics are pretty good for a 2008 game + Controls are pretty good (I played it with a controller) Cons: - Dialogue choices don't actually matter besides leveling abilities - Combat is extremely repetitive at first. Gets better the more you play and level aspects - Enemies have no health bars (including bosses) - Hard to know how to defeat a couple of bosses without googling it (especially the last one) - Have to go to start menu to check the map (which you will do alot). I feel like the map could have easily been mapped to a button. - Low replay value - Some glitches. I came across no game-breaking ones but I had to reload a couple times

title: rise of the argonauts
text: A solid action/RPG, but nothing really special. The gameplay is good, with the combat (which stresses making an opening and striking, rather than hacking away at an Hp bar), and skill systems (dedicating deeds to various gods, to gain their powers and favour) being of particular note. Voice-acting is acceptable (some is very solid, while some is just "ok"), although some conversations do not flow well.  Music is excellent. The setting is well-done; it is not not even close to being 100% true to the myths/history, but it works, and is certainly more accurate than the vast majority of "ancient Greece" games/movies these days. The games major drawbacks are a couple of annoying boss fights, graphics that are begining to show their age, and a number of irritating bugs (for me these were limited to some crashes to desktop when playing in certain areas, but others had reported worse). The game also has a pretty weak intro chapter, so it will get much better once you clear the first 30 minutes or so. Overall I would say Rise of the Argonauts is certainly worth playing, but only is you can get it cheap, and if you are willing to overlook its flaws.

title: rise of the argonauts
text: This game is an adventure game/action RPG set in ancient Greece in which you play the role of Jason, king and warden of Iolcus under the protection of Zeus himself. That sets the tone for the story. It's definitely a setting in which being a hero actually means something. The game itself is served by serviceable combat mechanics which are pretty common when it comes to hack and slash games at best it will remind you of a game like Kingdoms of Amalur but most of the time you can get by with simply mashing buttons (apart from the boss fights which will require you to study your foe to understand the pattern used by the boss to defeat him or her which is pretty standard gaming practice anyway). Some finishing moves are nice to behold and give a heroic feel to the fights. The game may not look incredibly good for 2017 and some of the textures can be a bit blurry but considering it was released in 2008 it's definitely not terrible and more importantly the art direction is rather solid with some nice touches in the background and a consistent use of assets in environments. Some faces seem to be recycled a bit too much but others really stand out in a good way. Animations are fine but they probably won't keep you up at night either. Foes usually look good and if you're into sandals you will probably like the way the main character looks (before playing this game I had no idea they made bikini armours for guys and Jason clearly likes showing his six pack abs so that may be a plus for the ladies). Voice acting is mostly good and sometimes excellent and the music is simply incredible. It sets the tone and give an epic vibe to the game (which doesn't come as a surprise considering that the composer was responsible for the music for the movie 300 and arguably the music wasn't the worst or the most controversial part). A great soundtrack is an important feature and that's an area in which this game shines. Considering the lack of games set in ancient mythic Greece especially when it comes to games that actually try to tell a story (I've enjoyed Titan Quest but it wasn't for the story) Rise of the Argonauts is an interesting title. It gets even better when it becomes obvious that despite its linearity (the game opens up a bit just like Bioware games in which you can explore several areas in a different sequence) it's actually a pretty good story for any fan of Greek mythology and computer RPGs. Of course the game takes some liberties with the myths and that can be irksome if you're a purist some of these changes annoyed me at first until I came to accept that the game was trying to keep things fresh and after a while I came to terms with that. The name dropping may annoy you and the fact that Achilles was supposed to be a baby at the time when Jason set off for his quest may annoy you just like the fact that some characters have slightly different roles like for instance Medea or even Perseus. In any case the writing is really good and there is plenty of dialogue (probably too much for some players) so it's a game that will require some patience and that may explain why it didn't do so well. What sets the game apart is the way experience is handled. After completing a quest or an achievement you get a deed that you can dedicate to a particular deity which allows you to get some points to buy skills in that god's skill tree. Each skill tree is focused on a different weapon type the mace, the spear, the sword and the shield so there is an incentive in focusing on a particular god. During dialogues you usually have four choices which are symbolized by a different icon so you can pick your lines by following a god's attitude for a particular situation. You have Ares (violent and brutal but straightforward and honest), Athena (mostly the just and sensible one but also the one who goes by the book), Apollo (compassionate, fair and dignified but also sometimes a bit proud) and Hermes (full of guile, mischief but also clever and manipulative). It gives some great flavour to the game. Quests make you feel like your choices actually matter which is good but in the end you're still moving along the main quest so it may be more of an illusion. Still the game offers enough leeway to actually feel less linear than it is and that's something that is really nice. Bottom line it's a good title for CRPG players who thirst for a mythological setting, it's not perfect (some backtracking is involved at times and there isn't much in the way of exploration) but it's much better than what the critics gave it credit for especially if you value the story above the rest. There is a caveat though and that's the fact that the game tends to crash a lot simply because it has to be run on a single core on modern computers. I used to have some pretty regular crashes but the game has been running very smoothly ever since I switched to a single core.

text: What I hate most in RPGs is that story in games of this genre are usually generic. And this game is not an exception - again you are the hero and must save the world. BORING! Then, as regards RPG genre, comes the world of the game. And here this game is quite good. Decent amount of NPCs and every one is doing something. During the day he can be a trader, in the evening he goes to the tavern or play a flute sitting near campfire etc., etc. This part of games Piranha Bytes always does well. Then comes the combat. And here the most controversal point of this game is burrowed. Theoretically the combat system is good. Attack chains, parries, blocks, dodge rolls - all is here. And at first glance the combat is skill based. But only at first glance, because implementation of the combat system is very poor. Parries are useless because activation time is same as for attacks, thus to land it properly you must just randomly press right mouse button. Dodges are also not great at all, because after performing one you will stay in place without ability to move yourself or even move camera for approximately 1 second. But this is not the worst moment of dodge rolls. The worst thing about it is that camera is locked on your opponent, so you can't dodge just left or right, you will always dodge around your opponent. And if you fight against few opponents at once, you will dodge right into the monsters that stay from the left or right hand from one, that you fight at this particular moment. So combat here is really "pain in one place", but it could be really good with proper implementation. OK, let's move further. Voice acting and sound effects are decent. Visuals are not bad, but all places of the game world look almost the same. With more divercity in flora types it will be much better. So, lets conclude - this game is not the best one in the genre, but not the worst one either. And if you want some adventures, then forward - the world of Risen awaits for its savior, and don't forget about princess!

text: Not easy in the least, but very well made. Great levels and enemy variety. Very well done sprites. Classes and abilities are perfect and feel powerful. Really large cache of items... that Stack! (like if you get an item that randomly shoots missiles when you fire, you can get it again and it stacks the effects) My first win was last night and took me 85min. (I got confused on the last level for ~25min. lol) Even so, it was VERY satisfying and i was proud. (even on so called 'easy') Great game, highly recommended. *EDIT* Forgot to mention the killer soundtrack! It's so perfect for this game.

title: risk of rain
text: +It's +It's to play with friends (knowledge about your router is required to open a port) +It has potential (UNLOCK ALL THE THINGS!!!!!) +   best gaym evurrrr  A retro rogue like game that has permanent death.   You can play with 4 people and maybe more with a hack.   It’s addicting fun to explore and discover several weapons, power ups and unlocks.  Great music and art!  Come play!  When you're not dying, it feels AWESOME. When you do die, even for reasons that should be total controller-throwing b.s., you forgive the game and try again. Because it never feels cheap.  Excellent game, great value, a really accessible rouge-lite if you want to get into the genre.  cool game  Have had a lot of fun with this game. Soundtrack is out of this world, and the game is punishing, but not artificially difficult. If you die, it's your fault. Artifacts let you add modifiers to your game, such as Glass, which gives you a 500% damage boost, but only 10% of your regular health. This, in addition to numerous character classes and items, makes the game have a lot of replay value, with each run being slightly different. Until you get the Command artifact, that is. My favourite element of the game is the difficulty slider. You genuinely feel rushed, as every few minutes the game gets harder, to the point where in later levels you will find yourself facing randomly spawned bosses from the first few levels. Or maybe that's a bug. I don't actually know :P But playing can become a real hassle later on, where you basically have to get a good ratio of items to time spent, and move on. You will not beat this game on your first try. That is a given. It is ball-crushingly hard, but in a way where if you play enough, the game becomes much more simple. Unlocking stuff is fun. Items are fun. Characters are fun. This review is a bit all over the place, I know, but I'd give this game a solid 9/10. It's the kind of game where I like to hop in, attempt a run or two, and go back to whatever I was doing. Just get someone to monitor your twitch chat. Standing still often will = death.
